newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes end slightly firmer, grades hit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes end slightly firmer, grades hit.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices ended slightly firmer Monday, trading in tight ranges while domestic grades continued to weaken on fundamental pressures.
"The grades were really getting beaten-up in there earlier," said a crude broker, noting the afternoon activity died down late following an active morning session.
March West Texas Intermediate/Cushing ended at $24.15-25 a barrel, steady to 5 cents higher from Friday.
Both the key sour and sweet barrels were hit equally hard, with West Texas Sour/Midland drifting down 10-20 cents from Friday to sell at a $2.30 discount to the WTI/Cushing.

Fundamentally, the picture for domestics remained bearish with abundant supplies, competitive foreign prices, poor margins and limited demand from refiners who have scheduled heavy maintenance programs in the first quarter of the year.
"There was some surprise at the weakness in the Midland, but everyone can see why the sours went lower," said a trader.
Sweets grades saw the Midland/WTI end at a 45 cts discount to the WTI/Cushing.
Light Louisiana Sweet/Empire ranged in the low 20's all day, selling late at 20-22 cts over the WTI/Cushing marker.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire ended steady to 10 cts weaker at a 35-45 cts discount to the benchmark.
Eugene Island was offered at $2.10 under the WTI/Cushing, and Postings Plus held around the $2.25 level.
